the-return-of-spring

Cupids and woodland figures dance in a flowery glade as spring returns. Bouguereau often painted fairy-tale scenes full of soft color and joyful movement. Nature wakes up after winter. It's a cheerful celebration of the season.
view-of-the-village

A young girl in a white dress sits in the shade of a tree, with a pretty village on a hill behind her. Bazille painted it at his family's home in Montpellier, in the south of France. The strong sunlight and shadows were new at the time. It's an early Impressionist masterpiece.
andromache-mourning-hector

A widow kneels at the bed of her husband Hector, a hero of the Trojan War, with her young son by her side. David painted this scene from Homer's Iliad. It has a stark, heartbreaking feeling. It helped earn him membership at the French Academy.
the-death-of-seneca

The Roman philosopher Seneca, ordered to take his own life by Emperor Nero, calmly dictates his last words to scribes as his friends weep. David painted a thoughtful, tragic scene early in his career. The story is about staying true to your values to the end. It's a powerful example of Neoclassical art.
la-encantadora-de-serpientes

A dark silhouette of a snake charmer plays a flute in a moonlit jungle, with glowing eyes and snakes coiled around. Rousseau said it was inspired by a friend's story of India. The painting is full of lush leaves painted in dozens of greens. It's a dreamlike masterpiece.
venus-rising

The goddess Venus rises from the sea, wearing a seashell like a hat, while cherubs frolic nearby. Gérôme was a great admirer of the classical world. He painted it late in his life. It's a lively picture of mythology.
view-of-arles-flowering-orchards

Blossoming orchards line the foreground, with the old town of Arles and its stone towers behind them. Van Gogh was captivated by the spring in Provence. The painting glows with white and pink flowers. It's a happy picture of a fresh season.
two-tahitian-women

Two women stand close together, one holding a bowl of flowers or fruit, in bright colors. Gauguin painted this in his later years in the Marquesas Islands. The flat, rich colors are a sign of his love of the Pacific. It's one of his best-known island paintings.
the-fourth-estate

A crowd of workers marches steadily out of the shadows toward us. Pellizza spent years on this painting. He called it 'The Fourth Estate' because it showed the working class as a new force in society. It became a symbol of workers' rights in Italy.
leonidas-at-thermopylae

The Spartan king Leonidas sits in calm readiness with his soldiers at the mountain pass of Thermopylae, preparing for a last stand against a vast Persian army. David painted the Spartans with heroic simplicity. In 480 BC, 300 Spartans and their allies held off the Persians for days. It's one of history's most famous last stands.
rejtan

A man throws himself at the doorway, begging for Poland not to be divided, while the nobles in the room look away. Matejko painted a moment from 1773, when Poland's neighbors carved up the country. It's a harsh message about betrayal. It's a famous national symbol.
regates-a-argenteuil

Sailboats with bright white sails glide across the Seine on a sunny day, with their reflections wobbling in the water. Monet lived at Argenteuil and painted boating there for years. The water ripples with strokes of color. It's one of his bright, breezy summer scenes.
the-gross-clinic

A famous surgeon pauses in an operating theater to explain a procedure to a room of students, his hand bloody. Eakins's honest picture showed modern science. Many in 1875 found the realism hard to look at. Today it's seen as one of the greatest American paintings.
the-apotheosis-of-homer

The Greek poet Homer sits at the center of a temple, crowned by a goddess of Victory, while the greatest writers, artists and thinkers from history gather around him. Ingres painted a tribute to the ancient world as a grand 'who's who.' The composition is very symmetrical and orderly. It was painted for a ceiling in the Louvre.
hip-hip-hurrah

A group of painters, writers and friends raise their glasses in a sunny garden in Skagen, in northern Denmark. Krøyer painted his colony of artist friends, including himself. The light is warm and the mood is joyful. It's one of the best-loved Danish paintings.
bonaparte-crossing-the-alps

Napoleon rides a mule on a mountain pass, looking rather calm, in a more realistic version of the heroic scene. Delaroche painted it in 1848 to show how it was in truth — a mule, not a prancing horse. It's a clever answer to David's famous idealized portrait. It reminds us that history can be told in different ways.
atropos

Giant figures float through the sky, with one holding scissors to cut the thread of life, like the Fates of Greek myth. It's one of Goya's Black Paintings on the walls of his home. The picture is also known as 'The Fates.' It's a spooky reflection on time and destiny.
nude-sitting-on-a-divan

A woman sits upright on a divan, painted with Modigliani's simplified, elegant, elongated shapes. He painted many such portraits in Paris in 1917. The curved lines and warm colors create a feeling of calm. It's an example of his unique style.
suprematist-composition

A tangle of colored rectangles and lines tilts and floats on a white ground, like objects in space. Malevich created Suprematism to show pure feeling in shapes. The painting seems to drift in all directions. It's an exciting piece of early abstract art.
the-open-window

An open window frames a view of boats in a harbor, with window boxes of flowers and bursts of pure color. Matisse painted this in the summer of 1905 at Collioure on France's southern coast. It's a famous Fauvist painting. It invites us to look out at a bright new view.
the-artist-s-garden-at-giverny

A path leads through arches of irises, daylilies and roses in Monet's colorful garden. He designed the garden himself and painted it for decades. The mass of flowers is painted in joyful strokes. It's a glimpse of the paradise he built.
the-rooks-have-returned

Dark birds perch in birch trees as a little church stands behind, and spring melts the snow. Savrasov painted this in a quiet village, and it became one of the most beloved Russian paintings. It's regarded as the start of a new feeling for Russian landscape. People love it for its quiet, simple beauty.
heroes

Three Russian knights on horseback, from folk tales, scan the horizon for danger. Vasnetsov painted Ilya Muromets, Dobrynya Nikitich and Alyosha Popovich, famous heroes. It took him nearly 20 years. Many Russian kids know this painting from school.
the-ballet-class

Young dancers stand and stretch in a practice studio, as the ballet master looks on. Degas loved to paint dancers behind the scenes, working hard. He painted many studies like this, with unusual views. It's one of his best-loved pictures.
lilac-bush

A bush of lilacs stands in the garden of an asylum in Saint-Rémy, with a blue sky. Van Gogh painted this in the spring of 1889. The soft purples and blues contrast with the green leaves. It's a quiet picture of beauty in a hard time.
interior

A man stands by a door, and a woman in a chemise sits sadly at the foot of a bed, in a dimly lit bedroom. Degas gave no title to explain the story, which makes people wonder. It's famous as a mysterious picture of tension between two people.
the-boy-in-the-red-vest

A young man in a red vest leans on his arm, painted in sculpted blocks of color. Cézanne painted this model, an Italian youth, several times. Look at his unnaturally long arm — it's deliberate, for the balance of the composition. It's one of the most famous modern portraits.
pink-and-blue

Two sisters in pink and blue dresses stand side by side, smiling softly. Renoir painted the daughters of a Parisian banker, Alice and Elisabeth Cahen d'Anvers. The soft colors and curls give them a sweet charm. It's a very sweet double portrait.
the-favourites-of-the-emperor-honorius

A Roman emperor feeds his pet chickens, which he called by the names of cities, while an official brings news. In the legend, he cared more for his hens than for the news that Rome was falling. Waterhouse painted a rich scene of the late Roman Empire. It's a funny and surprising story.
view-of-the-sea-at-scheveningen

Dark waves roll under a gray sky, with a few small figures and boats on the beach. Van Gogh painted this on the Dutch coast in 1882, in the wind and sand. Tiny grains of sand are still stuck in the paint. It's an early, wild seascape.
mariana

A woman stretches her back after hours of needlework, in a room of rich blue and gold, with a stained-glass window. The painting is inspired by a poem by Tennyson about a woman waiting for a lover who doesn't come. Millais used glowing colors. It's a gorgeous Pre-Raphaelite painting.
the-pearl-and-the-wave

A young woman reclines on a wave, with a pearl in her hand, as the surf and spray curl around her. Baudry painted it at the Paris Salon of 1863. The Empress Eugénie bought it. It's a charming picture of a water spirit.
the-hanging-of-the-sigismund-bell-at-the-cathedral-tower-in-

In 1521 in Kraków, workers raise a giant bell by ropes into the cathedral tower, as the crowd and the king watch. The Sigismund Bell is still in the cathedral and still rings. Matejko painted the pride of the city. It's a lively picture of a big community project.
the-tribuna-of-the-uffizi

Dozens of gentlemen crowd into a famous gallery in Florence, studying paintings and statues from the Renaissance. Queen Charlotte commissioned Zoffany to paint the picture, and he squeezed in masterpieces from all over the museum. He arranged the artworks and people as he liked. It's a picture of a museum filled with art.
les-alyscamps

A long avenue of poplars glows with yellow and orange autumn light, with strolling couples. It was an ancient Roman cemetery in Arles, France. Van Gogh painted it in autumn 1888. The golden trees seem to dance.
adele-bloch-bauer-ii

A fashionable woman in a pink, patterned dress looks out in front of a bright, richly colored background. Klimt painted her a second time, years after his gold portrait. This one is colorful instead of golden. It sold for $88 million in 2006.
bocca-baciata

A woman holds a flower and an apple, with a golden background, her mouth beckoning. The title means 'the kissed mouth.' Rossetti used her red hair and rich fabrics in a daring new style. It started a new direction in his painting.
la-parisienne

A stylish young woman in a deep blue dress and a flowered hat looks out with a confident smile. Renoir painted it in 1874 in the first year of Impressionism. The blue fabric glimmers in the light. It's an elegant picture of the modern city.
the-sin

A woman stands in the shadows with a large snake draped over her shoulders, her eyes glowing. Franz von Stuck painted this as a symbol of temptation. It was a huge success, and he painted several versions. It is a dark and dramatic Symbolist painting.
madame-monet-wearing-a-kimono

A woman in a bright red Japanese kimono stands with a fan against a background of fans. Monet's wife Camille posed for it. Japanese art was a craze in Paris in the 1870s. It's a colorful, playful piece.
godiva

According to legend, Lady Godiva rode a horse through the town in protest of a harsh tax, and the townspeople kindly stayed indoors. Collier painted her in a hush of dignity. The tale is a famous English legend. It's a picture of courage.
the-lady-with-a-fan-the-artist-s-wife

A woman in a splendid blue satin gown holds a fan, with a calm smile. Roslin painted his wife Marie-Suzanne Giroust, a talented artist herself. The shimmering fabric is a marvel. It's one of the great portraits of the 1700s.
crab-on-its-back

A crab lies on its back, its claws and legs curled, in a few strokes of orange and green. Van Gogh was inspired by Japanese prints and painted it in Paris. It's a quick but lively study. It shows he could find wonder in simple things.
the-bathers

A large woman steps out of a pond as her companion watches, in a Realist take on a classical theme. When it was shown in 1853, critics and the emperor were scandalized. Courbet liked to shock. It's a famous painting about honesty and realism.
the-kiss-edvard-munch

A couple's faces merge into one in a dim room, beside a window with a glimmer of light. Munch painted several versions of the scene. The way the two become one is touching and mysterious. It's one of his best-loved paintings.
self-portrait-with-bandaged-ear

Van Gogh looks out with a bandage over his ear, wearing a fur cap and a thick coat, with a Japanese print behind him. He painted it after he hurt his ear in December 1888. It's a direct, honest picture of a difficult time. It's among the most famous self-portraits.
one-hundred-horses

A hundred horses graze, rest, swim and gallop across a long scroll, a mix of Chinese and Italian styles. Castiglione, an Italian monk painter at the Chinese court, painted it for the emperor. It shows how different art traditions can combine. It's one of the treasures of Chinese court art.
self-portrait-with-a-black-dog

A young Courbet sits in the countryside with his dog, leaning against a rock, looking out with confidence. He painted this when he was 23. The dark landscape gives the picture a moody feeling. It's an early display of his talent.
the-vale-of-rest

Two nuns in a convent graveyard at twilight, one digging a grave, the other sitting nearby. Millais painted it near London, with a sunset sky. The still, silent mood is unforgettable. It's a haunting view of quiet devotion.
